takeaway: Portal hypertension in cirrhosis opens portal-systemic anastomoses: haemorrhoids, oesophageal varices, caput medusae, the bare area of the liver and retroperitoneal connections.

lines.text: Cirrhosis causes portal hypertension, so the body opens channels between the portal and systemic veins.
Around the inferior rectum and anal canal, these form haemorrhoids.
At the umbilicus, a recanalised ligamentum teres gives caput medusae.
At the bare area of the liver, portal and systemic veins swell where they meet.
And in the retroperitoneum, veins of the gut join veins of the body wall.
Oesophageal varices complete the five anastomoses.
Every option is one of these connections, so the answer is All of the above.
